collection.description: A villager has been a healer for fifty years.

ask.text:
(Name) has been a healer for fifty years. (He/She) has set the bones of half the village and delivered the other half. But (his/her) hands have started to shake, and last week (he/she) mixed up two jars of leaves and gave a fisher a tea that made (him/her) sneeze for a day.
The other healers are too polite to say anything. The {@chief} isn't. "You've earned a rest," the {@chief} says. "Sit in the sun. Tell stories. Let the young ones do the work."
(Name) loves the work. Should (he/she) keep going, or step aside?

c1o1.text: One afternoon (name) sits down on the bench outside the healers' hut to rest (his/her) eyes, with a half-ground bowl of leaves in (his/her) lap, and doesn't get up again. The other healers find (him/her) there, peaceful, looking as if (he/she) has just dozed off in the sun. The whole village comes to the burial. Half of them were delivered by (him/her), and one after another, they say so.

c1o2.text: Knowing (his/her) time is short, (name) spends the season teaching. Every healer in the village gets dragged into the hut for lessons, every afternoon, whether they like it or not. (Name) is a strict and impatient teacher. By the end of the season, the young healers grumble that their heads are full. They are also much better healers.

c1.text: "I'll rest when I'm dead," says (name), and goes back to the healers' hut. (He/She) works the whole season, slowly, carefully, double-checking every jar...

c2o1.text: (Name) expected to miss it terribly. Instead, after a week of sitting in the sun, (he/she) finds (he/she) doesn't miss it at all. Not the smells, not the blood, not the night calls. When a young healer comes asking for advice, (name) waves (him/her) off. "Ask someone who still cares," (he/she) says, and goes back to dozing. The healers are a little hurt.

c2o2.text: (Name) takes to sitting at the cooking fire in the evenings and telling the stories of every birth, every broken bone, every fever (he/she) has seen in fifty years. It turns out (he/she) remembers them all, and most of them are funny, especially the ones about the people sitting right there. The village has never laughed so much.

c2.text: (Name) hangs (his/her) healer's bag on the hook by the door and walks out into the sun. The first morning, (he/she) doesn't know what to do with (his/her) hands...
